da-false-claim.evidence: unstable-atom-decay-channel.md:14-16 'Pick the unique optimal vertex x*_LP closest to an integer point'; :33-39 uniqueness argument
da-false-claim.notes: The 'unique optimal vertex closest to an integer point' is not well-defined: an LP can have an entire optimal face, and 'closest to an integer point' presupposes a selection rule not specified. The uniqueness claim is only shown 'generically (off a measure-zero boundary variety)', so the stated proposition ('the unique violated constraint is well-defined') overstates what the proof gives; defensible as 'generically unique' but the as-stated unconditional 'unique' is not proved.

da-vacuous.notes: The .lean discharges a content-free ': True := trivial' while the .md states a substantive uniqueness proposition. Per AGENTS.md §1a this is exactly the forbidden vacuous/self-trivializing disposition (def-disguised-True); the proposition is not formalized at all.

da-referee-verdict.notes: verdict: major-revisions. referee_argument: Two compounding defects. (1) Logical: the proposition title asserts unconditional uniqueness/well-definedness of the decay channel, but the proof only establishes genericity off a measure-zero boundary variety, and the bridge from a rounded LP-relaxation vertex to the ILP-infeasibility certificate is asserted, not proved (the 'unique optimal vertex closest to an integer point' is ill-posed since x=0 is always LP-optimal). (2) Formal: the Lean sibling is 'def ... : True := trivial' (AGENTS.md §1a forbidden vacuity) AND its .ts lean.ref ('decay_channel') does not match the declared name ('decay_channel_unique'), so the proposition is unformalized and the ref is broken. Restate as 'generically unique', supply the primal→dual certificate lemma, and replace the True stub with the real statement (sorry + -- Ref:) or a conjecture.
